reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in addressing the mismatch between coarse clip-level laughter annotations and fine-grained temporal event boundaries. The proposed framework uses fixed HuBERT and MAE encoders to extract audio and visual features respectively, then applies temporal softmax pooling with adaptive modality gating. This design allows for efficient, scalable temporal grounding without frame-level supervision. The softmax pooling aggregates modality-specific features over time, while the adaptive gating dynamically weights modalities based on their relevance to the laughter event. The resulting temporal scores enable precise onset/offset detection. The model's strength stems from its ability to learn from weak labels, which is critical in real-world applications where manual frame-level annotation is impractical. Failure modes include misalignment of audio-visual cues, insufficient modality discrimination, or poor generalization to unseen affective signals beyond laughter.
